spatial_claims.claim: C lies between A and B on straight line AB, so AB = AC + CB
CD is a segment set out equal to 2*AC (separate from AB)
E lies between C and D on segment CD, with CE as the greater segment of the extreme and mean ratio cut (CE > ED)
Application of 13.1: square on (CE + CD/2) = 5 * square on (CD/2), using CE as the greater segment of CD
CE + AC = AB (from equality of their squares and both being positive lengths)

configuration_map: The configuration consists of two independent line segments: (1) Segment AB with interior point C, dividing it into AC and CB. (2) Segment CD (equal to 2*AC) with interior point E from the extreme and mean ratio cut, dividing it into CE (greater) and ED (lesser). These two segments do not interact spatially; the proof connects them only through algebraic equalities of squared lengths. The key algebraic chain is: AB² = 5·AC² (given), (CE + AC)² = 5·AC² (from 13.1 and CD = 2·AC), therefore CE + AC = AB, therefore CE = CB.
pass_reason: The proof is essentially algebraic, working with equalities of squares of lengths. The spatial configuration is minimal: two line segments each with one interior point, with no complex geometric constructions, no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior arguments, and no circle-based reasoning. All spatial claims (two betweenness claims and one segment construction) are independently established, trivially consistent, and never interact in a way that could produce contradiction.
